title: Kernel-row indexed Fitting data and canonical base-changed presentations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module, $n,k\in\mathbf N$, and $\pi:R^{\oplus n}\to M$ an $R$-linear map from the finite free module [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $I_k(\pi)=R$ if $n\le k$. Otherwise define $I_k(\pi)$ as the ideal spanned by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the square submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] with $n-k$ distinct columns of all $(n-k)\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] whose rows $z_i$ satisfy $\pi(z_i)=0$. No surjectivity or finite-generation hypothesis on $M$ is needed to construct this ideal. For a homomorphism $R\to A$, the canonical base-changed finite-free map [def-weil-module-base-change] is $\pi_A:A^{\oplus n}\to A\otimes_R M$, obtained by composing the inverse of the standard finite-free tensor identification $A\otimes_R R^{\oplus n}\simeq A^{\oplus n}$ with $1\otimes\pi$; it sends the standard vector $e_i$ to $1\otimes\pi(e_i)$. The index $k$ is arbitrary, including zero, and $n=0$ is allowed.
